clue.text: Tolerate what could be churchwarden's source of drink?

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe, so the churchwarden could be a pipe

explanation.surface: A church official's private supply of drink, presented as something to be put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The churchwarden here is not a parish officer but a long clay tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpipe is an outdoor water tap on a vertical pipe, so it supplies water to drink.

clue.text: A group of kneelers has to be withdrawn — they get worn by feet

indicators.note: the word has is to be pulled out of the kneelers

parts.note: hassocks are cushions to kneel on in church

explanation.surface: Church kneeling cushions are being taken away because people rest their feet on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Hassocks are church kneeling cushions; withdrawing HAS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks are garments worn on the feet.

clue.text: Chain tsar in revolution? One might do it

indicators.note: letters in revolution are overturned and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Putting a tsar in chains during a revolution; some radical might do just that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the whole first half, chaining a tsar in a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist is a revolutionary opposed to all rulers, the kind of person who might shackle an emperor.

clue.text: Club with loud music sure ruined conversation

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub playing loud music

indicators.note: the ruined word is wrecked and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Loud music in a club certainly spoils any chance of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club with loud music' reads as part of the scene, but it is one piece of wordplay naming the kind of nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is talk or communication between people, a formal word for conversation.

clue.text: What could remove cricket in school is above disgusting

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the second

parts.note: a school of thought is a sect
repellent means disgusting

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the game of cricket at school is called vile.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the chirping insect, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect repellent drives away bugs, and a cricket is an insect.

clue.text: Foreign coach about to be suspended, with pain later, in Devon city

indicators.note: the pain goes in later on, further along the city's name
the first two pieces go in the Devon city

parts.note: Exeter is the county city of Devon in south-west England
C is short for circa, about
to hang is to be suspended
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A foreign sports coach is about to be dropped and will be hurting in Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate pieces go into the city: 'about to be suspended' first, near its start, and the pain 'later', just before its final letter. 'Coach' means a teacher here, not a bus or trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange teacher comes from abroad to teach while swapping posts with a local teacher, so is a foreign instructor.

clue.text: Object when family avoids thinking

indicators.note: if the word thinking avoids its family, that group of relatives is taken out

parts.note: taken as the full word THINKING
kin means family

explanation.surface: Someone stops thinking about an object whenever relatives appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' removes KIN from THINKING.
explanation.definitionFit: An object and a thing are both general words for an item or article.

clue.text: Fish kilometres south of high rocks

indicators.note: in a down clue being south of means coming below

parts.note: tors are high rocky outcrops, as on Dartmoor
K is short for kilometres

explanation.surface: Fish caught a few kilometres south of some rocky peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The torsk is a North Atlantic food fish related to the cod.

clue.text: What's permissible in the middle of Tirol wood

indicators.note: the permissible word goes in the middle letters
the middle of a word is all but its ends

parts.note: OK means acceptable or permissible

explanation.surface: Something allowed in the heart of the Tyrol forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' strips both ends from Tirol, and the permissible word then goes into that middle, not into the full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Iroko is a hard tropical African timber, often used as a teak substitute.

clue.text: Beg urgent works for old printer

indicators.note: letters that are worked are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to plead for urgent jobs from an old printing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing in Europe in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Charles found with sister's skeleton in car

parts.note: Chas is the short form of the name Charles
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: Charles and his sister discover a skeleton hidden in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a motor vehicle, its structural skeleton.

clue.text: Cover needed for vehicle to carry round orchestra

indicators.note: the vehicle carries the next two pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
R is the abbreviation for round
PO is the abbreviation of Philharmonic Orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra on tour needs a covered van to transport it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover needed for vehicle' looks like the whole definition, but the vehicle is the CART that holds R and PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is an open-sided roofed shelter giving a parked car some protection.

clue.text: Small city company's artistic technique

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A small firm in the city has its own artistic method.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postal districts start EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Secco is the method of painting murals on dry plaster, as opposed to fresco.

clue.text: Repressive measure of drug bust?

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
a broken machine is bust or down

explanation.surface: A police drug bust is held up as an example of heavy-handed policing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a severe official campaign to suppress some activity.

clue.text: At the start West Ham is really revelling in noise made by fans?

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the next five words is taken

explanation.surface: West Ham supporters are making a racket while their team does well.
explanation.walkthrough: The fans are not football supporters but electric fans, whose blades whirr.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is the continuous buzzing hum of spinning blades, such as a cooling fan's.

clue.text: What's not just immoral monster's home

parts.note: wrong means immoral
Loch Ness in Scotland is home to the legendary monster

explanation.surface: An unfair, immoral place for a monster to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongness is the quality of being unjust or improper, the opposite of justice.

clue.text: Performance of empty melisma during fiddle part

indicators.note: the emptied word sits during, that is within, the fiddle and part

parts.note: to rig is to fiddle or manipulate
a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: emptying the word melisma leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A singer performs a hollow vocal run in the middle of a violin passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like a violin to suit the music, but it means to rig; a melisma is a run of notes sung on one syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tiresome procedure, a fuss, which is also called a performance.

clue.text: Something floating at sea put in a mister is a source of perfume

indicators.note: the floating thing is put in among the next three words

parts.note: a berg is an iceberg floating at sea

explanation.surface: A floating object is sprayed into a perfume atomiser.
explanation.walkthrough: The mister is the title, MR, not a spray bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales, prized in perfumery as a fixative.

clue.text: Inaugurate girl in old ceremony

indicators.note: the girl goes in the ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
Gina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl takes part in an ancient ceremony that launches something.
explanation.definitionFit: To inaugurate is to begin or set up, which is to originate something.

clue.text: Shot photo sent immediately

indicators.note: something shot is broken or ruined, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A photo was taken and sent straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a photograph, but it signals that PHOTO SENT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the spot means doing it at once, without delay.

clue.text: One in cottage room has good living

indicators.note: One is placed in the cottage room

parts.note: a ben is the inner room of a Scottish cottage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lodger in a cottage room is living comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish word for the inner room of a two-roomed cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being is existence, the state of living, as in 'came into being'.

clue.text: Irregular mostly struggling to capture land's leader?

definitions.text: Irregular mostly struggling to capture land's leader?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters capture the land's leader, holding it inside
struggling letters are thrown about into a new order
most of the word is used, dropping its final letter
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An irregular fighter battling to seize a country's ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: IRREGULAR without its last letter gives IRREGULA, rearranged as GUERRILA around L, the first letter of land's.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular soldier waging war, often trying to overthrow a nation's ruler.

clue.text: Wipe out periods of history? End of statue

parts.note: eras are periods of history

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Should whole ages of history be erased because a statue is toppled?
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to remove completely, to obliterate or wipe out.

clue.text: Lift? Lug up is embraced by that

indicators.note: is goes inside, held by the reversed word
in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lug is informal British for ear

explanation.surface: A lift where someone must lug something upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' is slang for ear; 'that' points back to the reversed ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up.

clue.text: Wet fish keeping cool?

indicators.note: the fish keeps the word for cool inside it

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A wet fish is being kept chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainy weather is wet weather, marked by rainfall.

clue.text: Unknown part of farm turning out fine produce

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the fine letter is turned out of the field

parts.note: a field is part of a farm
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An unidentified field gives a good crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a noun about crops, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to produce or give, as a crop or investment does.

clue.text: Inspect sack returned where coal comes from

indicators.note: the word for sack is turned back to front

parts.note: to give someone the axe is to sack them
coal is dug from a mine

explanation.surface: Someone checks a sack sent back from a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to look closely at something in order to check or assess it.

clue.text: Right of pasture at this point is including land

indicators.note: the word for at this point includes the word for land, holding it inside

parts.note: here means at this point
to land something, such as a prize, is to bag it

explanation.surface: A grazing right, it seems, covers the land at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, herbage is the right to graze cattle on another person's land.

clue.text: What's among vegetableS WE'D Eat?

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the following words, across their joins

explanation.surface: A question about which vegetables we would choose to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals show where the answer lies, across the end of one word and into the next two.
explanation.definitionFit: A swede is a root vegetable, the yellow turnip, so it is among the vegetables people eat.

clue.text: Knotty construction in clues, this shows what tons will also do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a decorative knot shaped like a turban

definitions.text: in clues, this shows what tons will also do
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in crosswords, the head of Turk gives T, the letter that tons also abbreviates to

explanation.walkthrough: In crossword language a word's 'head' is its first letter, and T is also the standard abbreviation for tons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turk's head is an ornamental knot woven round a rope, resembling a turban.
